The residual bound is a monotone may-bound, not a completeness proof: it cannot admit a target that no materialised-address evidence names, and the fixpoint is over the linked image plus the resolved OpenSSL DSOs, not a whole-program call graph.
The analysis identity is over .text and the symbol table.  It is not a byte-for-byte reproducibility claim across toolchains and it does not cover data-section contents.
The dynamic-trace axis is absent unless a trace is supplied; its absence is recorded, not treated as evidence.

text.direct_edges: call/jmp with a resolved immediate target; PLT stubs resolved to their in-DSO definition
text.dynamic_trace: none in this batch; this is a static call-path result
text.got_edges: call/jmp *off(%rip) whose slot carries R_X86_64_GLOB_DAT or R_X86_64_JUMP_SLOT, resolved to the relocation symbol
text.limits: static may-bound analysis. An unresolved indirect site is recorded as unresolved, never as a direct edge. Provider dispatch (EVP_SIGNATURE / keymgmt) is not enumerated here. Function-level reachability is not a safety or timing result.
text.roots: all undefined dynamic symbols of ssh and sshd that are defined in libcrypto's .dynsym; 180 roots (some imported names are aliases, e.g. EC_POINT_get_affine_coordinates_GFp resolves to the dynsym alias EC_POINT_get_affine_coordinates)
text.symbols: full .symtab FUNC ranges (readelf -sW); 10427 function nodes with outgoing direct/GOT edges in the resulting graph
text.unresolved_indirect: register/object-field indirect transfers (method tables, function pointers); these are the may-bound edges, not counted as direct

invocation.limitation: compile lines and harness paths are recorded verbatim; the reachability method is recorded as a structured object

non_claims: A dudect t-statistic is not an attack, not a wall-clock claim and not a remote-timing claim; it is a distribution difference at the stated geometry and threshold.
A low t-statistic is not a proof of constant time. The control's low t only validates the instrument at this sensitivity.

ctgrind observes data-flow-dependent branches and address uses only. It does not observe cache behaviour, speculation, port contention or any microarchitectural effect, and it says nothing about data that was not marked undefined.
The Phase-18 2.000x / 4.769x ratios are a bounded work-independence screen, not evidence of the leakage mechanism; the mechanism is the mod_exp_core branch set and the inverse's division/shift work.
The reachability result is static. 'Not reachable by direct/GOT edges' is not 'not reachable in any execution'; the may-bound routes are recorded, and the provider segments were not resolved.
The absence of an ssh/sshd import of either symbol is consistent with the baseline and does not by itself establish unreachability.
The DH path executing mod_exp_core through BN_mod_exp_mont is not a safety or timing result; it is a shared-implementation observation.
No claim is made about any other primitive (RSA-private, EC scalar mul, AEAD tag, HKDF) in this batch.
